input.ask: Commit these test builder fixes to the branch?

content.text:
The dropdown bug and the missing borders had one cause. The test builder was written for Docusaurus and uses its colour variables, which the new site maps to Maester's colours in `site.css`. That file is only loaded on pages outside the docs, and the builder is a docs page. So on that page every border, and the dropdown's background, had no colour: no field outlines, and the option list was see-through.

**Fixes**
- **Colours:** I moved that mapping into [theme.css](website/src/styles/theme.css), which every page loads. Fields have borders again and dropdowns have a solid background, in light and dark mode.
- **Less help text in the form:** each field now shows only its label, an "Optional" marker where it applies, a small **?** button, the input and any errors. The description, "How to choose" rubric, "Not in the list?" notes and the Control field's numbered steps all moved into a help panel that slides in from the side. Two other sections work the same way: "Rate the test, not your tenant" and "Why is there no Tag field?".
- **Help panel:** the panel doesn't lock the page. You can keep picking values while you read the rubric, clicking another field's **?** switches the panel to that field, and Esc or × closes it.
- **Layout:** the builder used to switch to two columns based on the window width, so at about 1000px the form was squeezed into a narrow strip beside the sidebar. It now switches based on its own width, and below about 900px it uses one column.

**Where the panel opens:** I put it on the right, not the left you suggested. When the form and code are side by side, it covers only the code column, so the field you're asking about stays in view. A panel from the left would cover the sidebar and the left edge of the form, including the field labels. In one-column layouts it slides over the right side of the form. If you'd still prefer the left, it's a small change.

I checked it in the browser in light and dark mode at 1024px and 1440px, and there were no console errors. I also removed some old CSS rules that were left over from an earlier version and were pushing the "Optional" marker into the middle of the row. content.text:
The test builder now keeps you on the page when you open a guide, and products show their icons. The page is still running at http://localhost:3200/test-builder; refresh it to see these changes. I checked both at 1440px wide with no console errors. Nothing is committed yet.

**Guides in the side panel**
- Clicking a guide in the left sidebar ("Your first custom test", "Attribute rubric" and the others) opens it in the right-hand panel instead of leaving the page. The URL stays `/test-builder` and your form is kept. The guides look the same as on their own pages.
- A link from one guide to another opens in the same panel, links to a heading jump within the panel, and outside links open in a new tab. There's an "Open in a new tab" link in the panel header.
- The panel covers the code column and leaves the form in view, like the field help. Opening a guide replaces any field help that's showing.
- On narrow screens, where the sidebar is a pop-up menu, clicking a guide still goes to its page as before.
- Interactive parts of a guide, such as copy buttons on code blocks, won't work inside the panel, because the guide's scripts don't run there.

**Product icons**
- The icons are the same ones the report and the test catalog use. They show in the Product dropdown, the selected value and the Related products checkboxes. Products without an icon (none of today's list) would show their initials, as in the catalog.
- Features show their icons too, for example the Conditional Access shield, because those icons come from the same file.

import re

# per-item Remove buttons -> icon only
n_before=s.count('size="xs" aria-label={"Remove "')
s=re.sub(r'<Button variant="ghost" size="xs" aria-label=\{"Remove " \+ ([^}]+)\} onClick=\{([^\n]+)\}>\n(\s*)Remove\n(\s*)</Button>',
         lambda m: '<Button variant="ghost" size="icon" aria-label={"Remove " + '+m.group(1)+'} title="Remove" onClick={'+m.group(2)+'}>\n'+m.group(3)+'<DeleteIcon />\n'+m.group(4)+'</Button>', s)
assert s.count('<DeleteIcon />')==n_before, (n_before, s.count('<DeleteIcon />'))
# Add buttons with plus
for old,new in [
 ('''                  <Button onClick={add} disabled={!valid}>
                    {group.length ? "Add an alternative (or)" : "Add"}''','''                  <Button onClick={add} disabled={!valid}>
                    <PlusIcon />
                    {group.length ? "Add an alternative (or)" : "Add"}'''),

          Add another requirement (and)'''),

          Add an alternative (or)
        </Button>'''),

]:
    assert old in s, old

# platform icons

assert old in s

# authors
old='''<Input id="input-author" value={state.author} placeholder="your-github-handle" onChange={(e) => set({ author: e.target.value })} />'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,'''<GitHubPeople id="input-author" value={splitList(state.author)} onChange={(v) => set({ author: v.join(", ") })} />''')
old='''<Input id="input-contributor" value={state.contributor} onChange={(e) => set({ contributor: e.target.value })} />'''
assert old in s
s=s.replace(old,'''<GitHubPeople id="input-contributor" value={splitList(state.contributor)} onChange={(v) => set({ contributor: v.join(", ") })} />''')
s=s.replace('''hint={P.Author.description + " Separate several with commas. Authors are credited on the contributors page."}''','''hint={P.Author.description + " Search GitHub by name or handle; the lookup reads public profiles only. Authors are credited on the contributors page."}''')
open(p,'w').write(s)
EOF

input.recap: Add and remove buttons now have plus and delete icons, platforms show operating system icons, and Author and Contributors search GitHub's public profiles. All checked in the browser; nothing is committed yet.
input.ask: Commit the test builder changes to this branch?

content.text:
All three changes are working on http://localhost:3200/test-builder; refresh to review them. I tried each one in the browser and nothing is committed yet.

- **Add and remove:** remove buttons on single items (permissions, licences, ATT&CK techniques and framework requirements) are now a delete icon. Hovering shows "Remove". The add buttons ("Add", "Add an alternative (or)", "Add another requirement (and)") have a plus icon. "Remove requirement" and "Remove alternative" have the delete icon next to their text.
- **Operating systems:** Windows, Linux and MacOS have their logos next to the checkboxes. They come from the icon set the site already uses and match the text colour.
- **Author and Contributors:** typing a name or handle searches GitHub's public profiles and lists matches with their avatars. Selecting one adds it as a chip with the avatar and the person's name, for example "Merill Fernando @merill". The trash icon removes it. The generated code still writes the handles, for example `Author = 'merill'`.
  - A handle that doesn't exist on GitHub gets a red outline and "not found on GitHub". That's how the example's placeholder `your-github-handle` now shows.
  - Without signing in, GitHub allows a visitor about 10 searches a minute. If someone hits that limit, the list says so, and they can still type the full handle and choose "Add … as written".
  - The lookups go from the visitor's browser straight to GitHub.

I also fixed an older styling bug: every item in the searchable lists (the licence and framework lookups too) looked greyed out, as if disabled.

The Permissions field still has a few paragraphs explaining the format inline, the same kind of clutter I moved into the side panel for the other fields. I can move those into its help panel too.
Commit it
